title: `ward init` and project binding
description: Spec §7.1 and §11.2. Opaque project UUID in tracked .ward/project.json; binding to a canonical Git worktree root lives only in the encrypted vault. Unknown checkouts, copied IDs, nested repos, worktrees and moved paths never inherit a binding. Ward-managed CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md block preserves every other block.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T10: unknown project, copied project ID, nested repo, worktree, moved path and unregistered clone cannot silently inherit a binding
T22: repeated init preserves user content and peer blocks; malformed markers and escaping symlinks are conflicts, not overwrites

implementationNotes: Design decisions recorded in docs/adr/0005-project-binding-identity.md (new ADR). Two points the spec leaves open, decided here and reported to the orchestrator: (1) a binding names the canonical worktree root AND that directory's device+inode (bigint, decimal strings), because a path alone cannot distinguish a fresh clone from the checkout it replaced at the same path, and spec §7.1 requires new clones to be handled explicitly; (2) registration is interactive only — a non-interactive caller is refused (denied/4, binding_requires_terminal) before the vault key is read, and there is deliberately no non-interactive register flag; --no-register prepares files without authority. Two non-interactive-asymmetries worth knowing: bare 'ward init' from a non-tty exits 4 even when the checkout happens to be registered already (Ward never reads the vault to answer a question it was not asked), and 'ward init' with no vault exits 3 (vault_not_found) after the scaffold is written, so a developer runs setup and re-runs init. P0 gap filed in the ADR: no unregister/rebind command exists, so a path bound to another project is resolved from the repository side (restore or remove the manifest).
